from django.core.exceptions import PermissionDenied, ValidationError
from django.db import IntegrityError, connection, transaction
from django.db.models import ProtectedError

from app_projects import services
from app_projects.models import Action
from app_projects.test_access import AccessBase
from appEmp.models import empProfile


class ActionBase(AccessBase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.admin = self.person(self.org1, "zz_aadmin@example.com", role="admin")
        self.worker = self.person(self.org1, "zz_aworker@example.com", project=self.pa)
        self.mate = self.person(self.org1, "zz_amate@example.com", project=self.pa)
        self.stranger = self.person(
            self.org2, "zz_astranger@example.com", role="admin", project=self.pc
        )
        self.worker_p = empProfile.objects.get(user=self.worker)
        self.mate_p = empProfile.objects.get(user=self.mate)
        self.stranger_p = empProfile.objects.get(user=self.stranger)

    def new(self, **over):
        kw = {
            "project": self.pa,
            "actor": self.admin,
            "title": "Write report",
            "assignee": self.worker_p,
        }
        kw.update(over)
        return services.create_action(**kw)


class CreateTests(ActionBase):
    def test_admin_creates_action_with_org_uuid_and_event(self):
        a = self.new()
        self.assertEqual(a.organization_id, self.org1.id)
        self.assertEqual(a.status, "todo")
        self.assertIsNotNone(a.uuid)
        self.assertEqual(list(a.events.values_list("kind", flat=True)), ["created"])

    def test_plain_member_cannot_create(self):
        with self.assertRaises(PermissionDenied):
            self.new(actor=self.worker)

    def test_admin_of_another_org_cannot_create(self):
        with self.assertRaises(PermissionDenied):
            self.new(actor=self.stranger)

    def test_assignee_must_be_on_the_project(self):
        outside = self.make(self.org1, "zz_aoutside@example.com", project=self.pb)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.new(assignee=outside)

    def test_assignee_from_another_org_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.new(assignee=self.stranger_p)

    def test_inactive_assignee_rejected(self):
        empProfile.objects.filter(pk=self.mate_p.pk).update(is_active=False)
        self.mate_p.refresh_from_db()
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.new(assignee=self.mate_p)

    def test_archived_project_is_read_only(self):
        self.pa.archive()
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.new()

    def test_blank_and_overlong_titles_rejected(self):
        for title in ("   ", "x" * 201):
            with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
                self.new(title=title)

    def test_model_rejects_project_from_another_org(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            Action.objects.create(organization=self.org2, project=self.pa, title="x")


class SubtaskTests(ActionBase):
    def test_subtask_in_same_project(self):
        parent = self.new()
        child = self.new(title="Part 1", parent=parent)
        self.assertTrue(child.is_subtask)
        self.assertEqual(list(parent.subtasks.all()), [child])

    def test_subtask_of_subtask_rejected(self):
        parent = self.new()
        child = self.new(title="Part 1", parent=parent)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.new(title="Part 1a", parent=child)

    def test_parent_from_another_project_rejected(self):
        parent = self.new()
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            self.new(project=self.pb, assignee=None, parent=parent)

    def test_parent_cannot_be_itself_at_database_level(self):
        a = self.new()
        with self.assertRaises(IntegrityError):
            with transaction.atomic():
                Action.objects.filter(pk=a.pk).update(parent=a)


class StatusTests(ActionBase):
    def test_assignee_moves_status_and_done_sets_completed_at(self):
        a = self.new()
        services.change_status(a, "in_progress", self.worker)
        services.change_status(a, "done", self.worker)
        a.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(a.status, "done")
        self.assertIsNotNone(a.completed_at)
        services.change_status(a, "todo", self.admin)
        a.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertIsNone(a.completed_at)
        self.assertEqual(
            list(a.events.values_list("kind", flat=True)),
            ["created", "status", "status", "status"],
        )

    def test_other_team_member_cannot_change_status(self):
        a = self.new()
        with self.assertRaises(PermissionDenied):
            services.change_status(a, "done", self.mate)

    def test_invalid_status_rejected(self):
        a = self.new()
        for bad in ("abc", "", None, ["done"]):
            with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
                services.change_status(a, bad, self.admin)

    def test_same_status_writes_no_event(self):
        a = self.new()
        services.change_status(a, "todo", self.admin)
        self.assertEqual(a.events.count(), 1)

    def test_archived_project_blocks_status_change(self):
        a = self.new()
        self.pa.archive()
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            services.change_status(a, "done", self.admin)


class ReassignEditDeleteTests(ActionBase):
    def test_reassign_and_unassign(self):
        a = self.new()
        services.reassign(a, self.mate_p, self.admin)
        a.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(a.assignee_id, self.mate_p.pk)
        services.reassign(a, None, self.admin)
        a.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertIsNone(a.assignee_id)
        self.assertEqual(a.events.filter(kind="assignee").count(), 2)

    def test_reassign_needs_manager(self):
        a = self.new()
        with self.assertRaises(PermissionDenied):
            services.reassign(a, self.mate_p, self.worker)

    def test_update_changes_fields_and_writes_one_event(self):
        a = self.new()
        services.update_action(a, self.admin, title="New title", description="Secret")
        a.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(a.title, "New title")
        self.assertEqual(a.events.filter(kind="edited").count(), 1)
        with self.assertRaises(ValidationError):
            services.update_action(a, self.admin, status="done")
        with self.assertRaises(PermissionDenied):
            services.update_action(a, self.worker, title="Hacked")

    def test_delete_needs_manager_and_removes_subtasks(self):
        parent = self.new()
        child = self.new(title="Part 1", parent=parent)
        with self.assertRaises(PermissionDenied):
            services.delete_action(parent, self.worker)
        services.delete_action(parent, self.admin)
        self.assertFalse(Action.objects.filter(pk__in=[parent.pk, child.pk]).exists())


class IntegrityTests(ActionBase):
    def test_moved_or_deactivated_assignee_is_flagged_not_cleared(self):
        a = self.new()
        b = self.new(title="Other", assignee=self.mate_p)
        empProfile.objects.filter(pk=self.worker_p.pk).update(project=self.pb)
        empProfile.objects.filter(pk=self.mate_p.pk).update(is_active=False)
        self.assertEqual(
            {x.pk for x in services.actions_needing_reassign(self.pa)}, {a.pk, b.pk}
        )
        a.refresh_from_db()
        self.assertEqual(a.assignee_id, self.worker_p.pk)
        self.assertTrue(a.needs_reassign)

    def test_assignee_cannot_be_deleted(self):
        self.new()
        with self.assertRaises(ProtectedError):
            self.worker_p.delete()

    def test_description_is_encrypted_at_rest(self):
        a = self.new(description="Top secret plan")
        with connection.cursor() as cursor:
            cursor.execute(
                "SELECT description FROM %s WHERE id = %%s" % Action._meta.db_table,
                [a.pk],
            )
            raw = cursor.fetchone()[0]
        self.assertNotIn("Top secret plan", raw)
        self.assertEqual(Action.objects.get(pk=a.pk).description, "Top secret plan")

# Phase 2 checklist (encryption of personal and salary data)

## Done

- [x] Keys: `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS` (Fernet, newest first) and a separate
      `BLIND_INDEX_KEY`; the app refuses to start if either is missing or invalid.
- [x] Encrypted field types (text, multi-line text, decimal); stored values start
      with `enc1:`.
- [x] Fingerprints for Aadhaar (unique across all organizations) and phone.
- [x] Personal fields encrypted: Aadhaar, PAN, bank account, UAN, ESIC, phone,
      address (migrations 0064 to 0066).
- [x] Salary figures encrypted: Salary basic, HRA, PF and daily rate, and the
      wage register rate override (migrations 0067 to 0069).
- [x] Code paths moved off plain columns: duplicate Aadhaar checks, HR phone search
      (full number only), WhatsApp router, admin search.
- [x] Admin lockdown: only superusers see and edit the seven personal fields.
- [x] Duplicate Aadhaar gives a plain form error; bulk import skips a row the
      database refuses and carries on.
- [x] `rotate_encryption_keys` command (with `--dry-run`).
- [x] Fresh-database fix in migration 0056, so an empty database migrates.
- [x] Tests: `python manage.py test appEmp.test_phase2_salary appEmp.test_phase2_encryption`
      (23 tests).
- [x] Deployment notes: `docs/phase2_deployment.md`.

## Must be true before the final cleanup

- [x] Real-page check passed: HR employee list and phone search, profile edit,
      bulk import preview and confirm, salary page, salary edit, wage register
      screen, payslip PDF.
- [x] Fresh backup taken and checked with `pg_restore --list`.
- [x] Tests pass.

## Final cleanup (migration 0070): drop the old plain-text columns

Drops 12 columns. The app does not use them, but they still hold the original
readable values, so until they are gone the encryption does not protect data
at rest.

- Personal: `aadhar_no_legacy`, `pan_no_legacy`, `bank_account_no_legacy`,
  `uan_no_legacy`, `esic_no_legacy`, `phone_number_legacy`, `address_legacy`
- Salary and wage: `basic_salary_legacy`, `hra_legacy`, `pf_legacy`,
  `daily_rate_legacy`, `rate_override_legacy`

This cannot be undone from inside the database; the only way back is a backup.

- [x] Migration 0070 written and applied
- [x] Models cleaned (the legacy field lines removed)
- [x] Tests pass and pages checked again
- [ ] Old plain-text dumps deleted from `~/db_backups/` once you are sure
      (`postgres_before_phase2_5a.dump`, `postgres_before_phase2_5b.dump`,
      `postgres_before_salary_enc.dump`, and any older ones)

## Before the first production release

`.github/workflows/deploy.yml` deploys on every push to `main` and runs `migrate`
with no backup and no key check. **Do not push `main` until these are done.**

- [ ] `deploy.yml`: add `script_stop: true` so a failed step stops the deploy.

# Phase 4 deployment notes

## Every deploy that includes projects

1. Back up the database.
2. python manage.py migrate
3. python manage.py sync_project_permissions

Step 3 adds view_all_projects and manage_projects to the ORG_ADMIN and
HR_ADMIN groups. Without it, existing admins in those groups cannot see
or manage projects. Owners, admins and managers by organization role are
not affected, because project access also passes by role. The command only
adds permissions and is safe to run again.

New organizations get the permissions automatically through
ensure_org_admin_group.

## Migrations so far

- app_projects 0001: Project table
- appEmp 0071: empProfile.project (nullable)
- app_projects 0002: project permissions (no table change)

==> ./docs/phase2_deployment.md <==
# Phase 2 deployment notes (encrypted personal data)

Applies to: appEmp migrations 0064 to 0070.
Assumes the app runs from a checkout of this repo on EC2, loads `.env.production`
(`DJANGO_ENV=production`), and uses PostgreSQL (local, or RDS).

## What changed and why it matters

Aadhaar, PAN, bank account, UAN, ESIC, phone and address are now stored
encrypted. Two secrets control this, and the app will not start without them:

- `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS`: one or more Fernet keys, comma separated, newest first.
  The first key encrypts. Every listed key can decrypt.
- `BLIND_INDEX_KEY`: a separate secret used for the fingerprints that make duplicate
  Aadhaar checks and phone search possible. At least 32 characters.

**If `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS` is lost, the encrypted data cannot be recovered.**
**If `BLIND_INDEX_KEY` is changed, every fingerprint stops matching.** Treat both as
long-lived secrets. A fingerprint rebuild is possible (values can still be
decrypted), but there is no command for it yet.

## Generating and storing the keys

Run once, on any machine with the project installed. Do not run it in a shared
terminal session or paste the output into chat, tickets or logs.

    python -c "from cryptography.fernet import Fernet; print(Fernet.generate_key().decode())"

    python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_urlsafe(48))"

The first command gives the encryption key, the second the blind-index key.

Where they live:

- On the server: only in `.env.production`, owned by the app user, `chmod 600`.
- A backup copy of both keys in a password manager or a secrets service (for
  example AWS Secrets Manager). **Keep it somewhere other than the database
  backups.** A backup that sits next to its own key protects nothing.
- Never in git. `.env.example` holds variable names with placeholder text only.

## Startup errors and what they mean

| Message starts with | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS is not set` | The variable is missing or empty in the env file the server loaded. Check `DJANGO_ENV=production` and the file name. |
| `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS entry #N is not a valid Fernet key` | Entry number N was mistyped or cut off. |
| `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS contains a duplicate key` | The same key appears twice. |
| `BLIND_INDEX_KEY is missing or shorter than 32 characters` | Missing, empty or too short. |
| `BLIND_INDEX_KEY must be different from every encryption key` | The two secrets must be different values. |

A value that cannot be decrypted at runtime raises an error that names the field and
row but never the value or a key. That means the wrong key is loaded or the stored
data is damaged.

## Deploying to an existing server that already has data

The migrations rename columns, so the old code cannot run against the new schema.
Plan for a short stop.

1. Stop the app (the way you normally do).
2. Back up, verify the backup, and copy it off the server:

        pg_dump -h DB_HOST -U DB_USER -Fc DB_NAME -f ~/before_phase2.dump
        pg_restore --list ~/before_phase2.dump | head -20

3. Add `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS` and `BLIND_INDEX_KEY` to `.env.production`.
4. Pull the code and install requirements. `cryptography` must be in
   `requirements.txt`.
5. Apply migrations and check:

        python manage.py migrate
        python manage.py check

6. Start the app.
7. Verify:

        python manage.py rotate_encryption_keys --dry-run

   Every field should report all values "already on newest key" and `rotated=0`.
   Then confirm the stored values are ciphertext:

        psql -h DB_HOST -U DB_USER DB_NAME -c "SELECT count(*) AS total, count(aadhar_no) AS aadhaar_set, count(*) FILTER (WHERE aadhar_no LIKE 'enc1:%') AS aadhaar_encrypted FROM \"appEmp_empprofile\";"

   `aadhaar_set` and `aadhaar_encrypted` must be equal. Then log in and check the HR
   employee list, a phone search, a profile edit and a bulk import preview.

Do not run `makemigrations` on the server.

### Rolling back

Restore the backup from step 2 and deploy the previous code. Do not use
`migrate appEmp 0065` for a rollback after real use: edits made after the switch
exist only in the encrypted columns, and the restored plain columns would be stale.

## Building a new RDS database

Do not run `migrate` on an empty RDS database and expect a working system. A fresh
database has no `yugaamAi` organization, so the copy-from-default steps for new
organizations have nothing to copy. Build it from a dump instead:

1. Create the RDS PostgreSQL instance (same major version as the source), turn on
   storage encryption at creation (it cannot be added later), keep automated
   backups on, and let the security group accept connections only from the EC2
   instance.
2. Create the database and user.
3. Take a custom-format dump from the source **after migration 0066 has been
   applied there**, then restore:

        pg_restore --no-owner --no-privileges -h RDS_HOST -U RDS_USER -d RDS_DB before_move.dump

4. Set `DB_NAME`, `DB_USER`, `DB_PASSWORD`, `DB_HOST`, `DB_PORT` in
   `.env.production`, with the **same** `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS` and
   `BLIND_INDEX_KEY` as the source. Different keys would make the data unreadable.
5. Run `python manage.py migrate`. It should report nothing to apply.
6. Run the verification in step 7 above.

If the connection fails with an SSL error, RDS is requiring SSL. The database
settings may then need `OPTIONS: {"sslmode": "require"}`.

## Rotating the encryption key

Reasons: a scheduled rotation, or someone who had access to the key leaving.

1. Generate a new key.
2. Put it **first** and keep the old one after it, for example
   `FIELD_ENCRYPTION_KEYS=NEWKEY,OLDKEY`, then restart every app process. Never
   replace the only key in place.
3. Back up the database.
4. Run `python manage.py rotate_encryption_keys --dry-run` and read the counts.
5. Run `python manage.py rotate_encryption_keys`. It runs in one transaction,
   re-encrypts each value, and rolls back if any value is not readable with the new
   key alone.
6. Run the dry run again. It must report `rotated=0`.
7. Keep the old key stored safely for as long as any backup made before the
   rotation might need restoring. Only then remove it from the env file.

`BLIND_INDEX_KEY` is not touched by rotation.

## Not finished yet

- Migration 0070 drops the old plain-text columns. It cannot be reversed from inside
  the database, so take the backup in step 2 before deploying.
- Database dumps made before this phase contain plain text. Keep them only as
  long as you need them, and protect or delete them after that.

## Tests

Run these on a development machine, not against the production database:

    python manage.py test appEmp.test_phase2_encryption

==> ./.github/workflows/deploy.yml <==
name: Deploy to EC2

on:
  push:
    branches:
      - main

jobs:
  deploy:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
      - name: Deploy to EC2 via SSH
        uses: appleboy/ssh-action@v1.0.3
        with:
          host: ${{ secrets.EC2_HOST }}
          username: ${{ secrets.EC2_USER }}
          key: ${{ secrets.EC2_SSH_KEY }}
          script: |
            set -e
            cd ${{ secrets.EC2_PROJECT_PATH }}
            source venv/bin/activate
            git pull origin main
            pip install -r requirements.txt
            python manage.py check
            python manage.py migrate --noinput
            python manage.py collectstatic --noinput
            sudo systemctl restart gunicorn
            sleep 2
            sudo systemctl is-active --quiet gunicorn || (sudo journalctl -u gunicorn -n 25 --no-pager && exit 1)

                {% if field.field.widget.input_type == 'password' %}
                <div class="sky-password-wrap">
                    {{ field }}
                    <button type="button" class="sky-pw-toggle" data-target="{{ field.id_for_label }}" title="Show/Hide password">
                        <i class="sky-eye-icon"></i>
                    </button>
                    <button type="button" class="sky-pw-copy" data-target="{{ field.id_for_label }}" title="Copy password">
                        <i class="sky-copy-icon"></i>
                    </button>
                </div>
                {% else %}
                    {{ field }}
                {% endif %}

                {% if field.errors %}
                    <div class="sky-form-error">{{ field.errors|striptags }}</div>
                {% endif %}
            </div>
            {% endfor %}
            <button type="submit" class="sky-auth-submit">Register</button>
        </form>
    </div>
</div>

{% block extra_js %}
<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
    // Eye toggle: show/hide password
    document.querySelectorAll('.sky-pw-toggle').forEach(function (btn) {
        btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            var input = document.getElementById(btn.dataset.target);
            if (!input) return;
            if (input.type === 'password') {
                input.type = 'text';
                btn.classList.add('is-visible');
            } else {
                input.type = 'password';
                btn.classList.remove('is-visible');
            }
        });
    });

    // Copy password to clipboard
    document.querySelectorAll('.sky-pw-copy').forEach(function (btn) {
        btn.addEventListener('click', function () {
            var input = document.getElementById(btn.dataset.target);
            if (!input || !input.value) return;

            navigator.clipboard.writeText(input.value).then(function () {
                var original = btn.title;
                btn.title = 'Copied!';
                btn.classList.add('is-copied');
                setTimeout(function () {
                    btn.title = original;
                    btn.classList.remove('is-copied');
                }, 1500);
            });
        });
    });
});
</script>
{% endblock %}

<script>

document.addEventListener(
    "DOMContentLoaded",
    function () {

        const toggle =
            document.querySelector(
                ".password-toggle"
            );

        if (!toggle) {
            return;
        }

        const wrapper =
            toggle.closest(
                ".password-input-wrap"
            );

        const input =
            wrapper.querySelector("input");

        toggle.addEventListener(
            "click",
            function () {

                if (
                    input.type === "password"
                ) {

                    input.type = "text";

                    toggle.textContent =
                        "Hide";

                    toggle.setAttribute(
                        "aria-label",
                        "Hide password"
                    );

                } else {

                    input.type =
                        "password";

                    toggle.textContent =
                        "Show";

                    toggle.setAttribute(
                        "aria-label",
                        "Show password"
                    );

                }

            }
        );

    }
);

</script>

        {% if form.non_field_errors %}
        <div class="sky-auth-error-banner">
            {% for error in form.non_field_errors %}{{ error }}{% endfor %}
        </div>
        {% endif %}

            {% csrf_token %}
            {% for field in form %}
            <div class="sky-auth-field">
                <label for="{{ field.id_for_label }}">{{ field.label }}</label>
                {{ field }}
                {% if field.help_text %}
                    <div class="sky-help-text">{{ field.help_text|safe }}</div>
                {% endif %}
                {% if field.errors %}
                    <div class="sky-form-error">{{ field.errors|striptags }}</div>
                {% endif %}
            </div>

    </div>
</div>

<script>
    function prepareRejectForm(form) {
        const reason = prompt('Reason for rejecting this document (optional):', '');
        if (reason === null) {
            // User cancelled the prompt
            return false;
        }
        if (!confirm('Reject this document? The employee will need to re-upload it.')) {
            return false;
        }
        form.querySelector('input[name="rejection_reason"]').value = reason;
        return true;
    }
</script>

<script>

document.addEventListener(
    "DOMContentLoaded",
    function () {

        const modeField = document.getElementById(
            "id_leave_start_mode"
        );

        const dateWrapper = document.getElementById(
            "selected-date-wrapper"
        );

        const selectedDate = document.getElementById(
            "id_selected_leave_start_date"
        );


        function updateSelectedDateVisibility() {

            if (
                modeField.value === "SELECTED_DATE"
            ) {

                dateWrapper.style.display = "";

            } else {

                dateWrapper.style.display = "none";

                if (selectedDate) {
                    selectedDate.value = "";
                }

            }

        }


        updateSelectedDateVisibility();


        modeField.addEventListener(
            "change",
            updateSelectedDateVisibility
        );

    }
);

</script>

#!/usr/bin/env python
"""Django's command-line utility for administrative tasks."""
import os
import sys


def main():
    """Run administrative tasks."""
    os.environ.setdefault('DJANGO_SETTINGS_MODULE', 'projSkySource.settings')
    try:
        from django.core.management import execute_from_command_line
    except ImportError as exc:
        raise ImportError(
            "Couldn't import Django. Are you sure it's installed and "
            "available on your PYTHONPATH environment variable? Did you "
            "forget to activate a virtual environment?"
        ) from exc
    execute_from_command_line(sys.argv)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

==> ./app_organizations/migrations/0002_seed_default_organization.py <==
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import migrations

DEFAULT_ORG_NAME = "yugaamAi"


def seed_default_organization(apps, schema_editor):
    User = apps.get_model(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL)
    Organization = apps.get_model("app_organizations", "Organization")
    OrganizationMember = apps.get_model("app_organizations", "OrganizationMember")
    EmpProfile = apps.get_model("appEmp", "empProfile")

    owner = User.objects.filter(is_superuser=True).order_by("id").first()
    if owner is None:
        if not User.objects.exists():
            # Fresh database: nothing to seed.
            return
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Cannot seed the default organization: users exist but no superuser "
            "was found. Create one (python manage.py createsuperuser) and re-run migrate."
        )

    org, _ = Organization.objects.get_or_create(
        name=DEFAULT_ORG_NAME,
        defaults={"created_by": owner},
    )

    manager_user_ids = set(
        EmpProfile.objects.filter(manager__isnull=False)
        .values_list("manager__user_id", flat=True)
    )

    for user in User.objects.all().order_by("id"):
        if user.id == owner.id:
            role = "owner"
        elif user.is_superuser:
            role = "admin"
        elif user.id in manager_user_ids:
            role = "manager"
        else:
            role = "member"

        OrganizationMember.objects.get_or_create(
            user=user,
            defaults={"organization": org, "role": role},
        )


def unseed_default_organization(apps, schema_editor):
    Organization = apps.get_model("app_organizations", "Organization")
    OrganizationMember = apps.get_model("app_organizations", "OrganizationMember")

    org = Organization.objects.filter(name=DEFAULT_ORG_NAME).first()
    if org:
        OrganizationMember.objects.filter(organization=org).delete()
        org.delete()


class Migration(migrations.Migration):

    dependencies = [
        migrations.swappable_dependency(settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL),
        ("app_organizations", "0001_initial"),
        ("appEmp", "0051_wageregisterentry"),
    ]

    operations = [
        migrations.RunPython(seed_default_organization, unseed_default_organization),
    ]

==> ./app_organizations/services.py <==
from django.contrib.auth import get_user_model
from django.core.exceptions import ValidationError
from django.core.validators import validate_email
from django.db import transaction

from .models import Organization, OrganizationMember
from .seed import (
    copy_import_config,
    ensure_org_admin_group,
    seed_org_defaults,
)


def create_organization(
    *, name, owner_email, owner_first_name, owner_last_name="", created_by
):
    """
    Create an organization with its first owner, all or nothing.

    Raises ValueError with a message safe to show the person using the form.
    Returns (organization, owner_user).
    """
    User = get_user_model()

    name = (name or "").strip()
    owner_email = (owner_email or "").strip()
    owner_first_name = (owner_first_name or "").strip()
    owner_last_name = (owner_last_name or "").strip()

    if not name:
        raise ValueError("Organization name is required.")
    if not owner_first_name:
        raise ValueError("Owner first name is required.")
    if not owner_email:
        raise ValueError("Owner email is required.")
    try:
        validate_email(owner_email)
    except ValidationError:
        raise ValueError("Enter a valid owner email address.")

    if Organization.objects.filter(name__iexact=name).exists():
        raise ValueError("An organization with this name already exists.")
    if User.objects.filter(email__iexact=owner_email).exists():
        raise ValueError("An account with this email already exists.")

    with transaction.atomic():
        org = Organization.objects.create(name=name, created_by=created_by)

        # Masters first, so the owner gets the default shift from the signal.
        seed_org_defaults(org)
        copy_import_config(org)
        group = ensure_org_admin_group()

        owner = User(
            username=owner_email,
            email=owner_email,
            first_name=owner_first_name,
            last_name=owner_last_name,
        )
        owner.set_unusable_password()
        owner._organization = org
        owner.save()

        membership = OrganizationMember.objects.get(user=owner)
        if membership.organization_id != org.id:
            raise RuntimeError("Owner was attached to the wrong organization.")
        membership.role = "owner"
        membership.save(update_fields=["role"])

        owner.groups.add(group)

    return org, owner

==> ./app_organizations/models.py <==
from django.conf import settings
from django.db import models


class Organization(models.Model):
    name = models.CharField(max_length=150)
    created_by = models.ForeignKey(
        settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL,
        on_delete=models.PROTECT,
        related_name="organizations_created",
    )
    created_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.name


class OrganizationMember(models.Model):
    ROLE_CHOICES = [
        ("owner", "Owner"),
        ("admin", "Admin"),
        ("manager", "Manager"),
        ("member", "Member"),
    ]

    organization = models.ForeignKey(
        Organization, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name="members"
    )
    # OneToOne: in Pro a user belongs to exactly one organization.
    user = models.OneToOneField(
        settings.AUTH_USER_MODEL,
        on_delete=models.CASCADE,
        related_name="organization_membership",
    )
    role = models.CharField(max_length=20, choices=ROLE_CHOICES, default="member")
    joined_at = models.DateTimeField(auto_now_add=True)

    def __str__(self):
        return f"{self.user.username} - {self.organization.name} ({self.role})"

from datetime import time

SHIFTS = [
    {"name": "General Shift", "start_time": time(9, 0), "end_time": time(18, 0),
     "is_night_shift": False, "grace_period_minutes": 10, "make_default": True},
    {"name": "Night Shift", "start_time": time(22, 0), "end_time": time(6, 0),
     "is_night_shift": True, "grace_period_minutes": 10, "make_default": False},
]

LEAVE_TYPES = [
    {"name": "Casual Leave", "code": "CL", "is_paid": True,
     "allow_half_day": True, "requires_document": False},
    {"name": "Earned Leave", "code": "EL", "is_paid": True,
     "allow_half_day": True, "requires_document": False},
    {"name": "Loss of Pay", "code": "LOP", "is_paid": False,
     "allow_half_day": False, "requires_document": False},
    {"name": "Sick Leave", "code": "SL", "is_paid": True,
     "allow_half_day": True, "requires_document": True},
]

DOCUMENT_TYPES = [
    {"name": "Aadhar Card", "description": "Government-issued Aadhar identity card"},
    {"name": "Offer Letter", "description": "Signed offer letter"},
    {"name": "PAN Card", "description": "Permanent Account Number card"},
    {"name": "Resume", "description": "Employee resume / CV"},
]

WORK_SCHEDULES = [
    {"name": "Standard 5-Day Week",
     "monday": True, "tuesday": True, "wednesday": True,
     "thursday": True, "friday": True, "saturday": False, "sunday": False,
     "make_default": True},
]


def _seed(model, org, rows):
    """Create missing rows for this org, matched on name. Returns count created."""
    created = 0
    has_default = (
        hasattr(model, "is_default")
        and model.objects.filter(organization=org, is_default=True).exists()
    )
    for row in rows:
        row = dict(row)
        name = row.pop("name")
        make_default = row.pop("make_default", False)
        if make_default and not has_default:
            row["is_default"] = True
        elif "make_default" in rows[0] or make_default:
            row["is_default"] = False
        _, was_created = model.objects.get_or_create(
            organization=org, name=name, defaults=row
        )
        if was_created:
            created += 1
            if row.get("is_default"):
                has_default = True
    return created


def seed_org_defaults(org):
    """
    Give a new organization its starting masters.
    Safe to run twice: existing rows (same name in this org) are left alone.
    Returns a dict of how many rows were created per master.
    """
    from appEmp.models import (
        DocumentTypeMaster,
        LeaveTypeMaster,
        ShiftMaster,
        WorkSchedule,
    )

    return {
        "shifts": _seed(ShiftMaster, org, SHIFTS),
        "leave_types": _seed(LeaveTypeMaster, org, LEAVE_TYPES),
        "document_types": _seed(DocumentTypeMaster, org, DOCUMENT_TYPES),
        "work_schedules": _seed(WorkSchedule, org, WORK_SCHEDULES),
    }


IMPORT_CONFIG_FIELDS = (
    "column_label",
    "display_name",
    "target_model",
    "data_type",
    "is_required",
    "validation_regex",
    "validation_message",
    "order",
    "is_active",
)


def copy_import_config(org, source_org=None):
    """
    Copy the employee-import field config rows from source_org to org.
    source_org defaults to the first organization by id (yugaamAi).
    Safe to run twice: rows are matched on (organization, field_key).
    Returns the number of rows created.
    """
    from appEmp.models import EmployeeImportFieldConfig
    from .models import Organization

    if source_org is None:
        source_org = Organization.objects.order_by("id").first()
    if source_org is None or source_org.pk == org.pk:
        return 0

    created = 0
    for row in EmployeeImportFieldConfig.objects.filter(organization=source_org):
        defaults = {name: getattr(row, name) for name in IMPORT_CONFIG_FIELDS}
        _, was_created = EmployeeImportFieldConfig.objects.get_or_create(
            organization=org,
            field_key=row.field_key,
            defaults=defaults,
        )
        if was_created:
            created += 1
    return created


ORG_ADMIN_GROUP = "ORG_ADMIN"

ORG_ADMIN_PERMISSIONS = (
    "view_hr_dashboard",
    "manage_employees",
    "manage_attendance",
    "manage_leave_balance",
    "manage_salary",
    "review_leave",
    "review_attendance_exception",
    "review_finance_noc",
    "view_all_clearance_requests",
    "apply_clearance_for_employee",
    "initiate_employee_exit",
    "finalize_employee_exit",
)

ORG_ADMIN_PROJECT_PERMISSIONS = (
    "view_all_projects",
    "manage_projects",
)


def ensure_org_admin_group():
    """
    Return the ORG_ADMIN group, creating it if needed, holding exactly the
    12 custom appEmp permissions the app checks, plus the 2 project permissions (no model add/change/delete/view
    permissions, nothing for Django's own tables).
    Raises RuntimeError, creating nothing, if any permission does not exist.
    """
    from django.contrib.auth.models import Group, Permission

    perms = Permission.objects.filter(
        content_type__app_label="appEmp",
        codename__in=ORG_ADMIN_PERMISSIONS,
    )
    found = set(perms.values_list("codename", flat=True))
    missing = set(ORG_ADMIN_PERMISSIONS) - found
    if missing:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Missing appEmp permissions: " + ", ".join(sorted(missing))
        )

    project_perms = Permission.objects.filter(
        content_type__app_label="app_projects",
        codename__in=ORG_ADMIN_PROJECT_PERMISSIONS,
    )
    project_found = set(project_perms.values_list("codename", flat=True))
    project_missing = set(ORG_ADMIN_PROJECT_PERMISSIONS) - project_found
    if project_missing:
        raise RuntimeError(
            "Missing app_projects permissions: " + ", ".join(sorted(project_missing))
        )

    group, _ = Group.objects.get_or_create(name=ORG_ADMIN_GROUP)
    group.permissions.set(list(perms) + list(project_perms))
    return group

    list_display = ("user", "organization", "role", "joined_at")
    list_filter = ("organization", "role")
    search_fields = ("user__username", "user__email")
    list_select_related = ("user", "organization")

    def get_readonly_fields(self, request, obj=None):
        # Changing org here would leave the employee profile in the old org.
        if obj is not None:
            return ("organization", "user")
        return ()

    def has_add_permission(self, request):
        # Every new user gets a membership automatically (appEmp signal).
        return False

==> ./app_organizations/utils.py <==
from functools import wraps

from django.contrib.auth.views import redirect_to_login
from django.core.exceptions import PermissionDenied

from .models import OrganizationMember

ALL_ROLES = ("owner", "admin", "manager", "member")


def get_user_membership(user):
    """The user's single OrganizationMember row, or None."""
    return (
        OrganizationMember.objects
        .select_related("organization")
        .filter(user=user)
        .first()
    )


def require_org_role(allowed_roles=None):
    """
    Allow the view only for users whose role in their own org is in
    allowed_roles (default: any role).

    - Anonymous users are sent to the login page.
    - Superusers always pass.
    - Everyone else must have request.current_org (set by the
      middleware) and a membership in that same org, with an allowed role.
    - Sets request.org_membership. Never changes request.current_org.
    """
    if allowed_roles is None:
        allowed_roles = ALL_ROLES

    def decorator(view_func):
        @wraps(view_func)
        def _wrapped_view(request, *args, **kwargs):
            user = request.user
            if not user.is_authenticated:
                return redirect_to_login(request.get_full_path())

            membership = get_user_membership(user)

            if user.is_superuser:
                request.org_membership = membership
                return view_func(request, *args, **kwargs)

            org = getattr(request, "current_org", None)
            if (
                org is None
                or membership is None
                or membership.organization_id != org.id
                or membership.role not in allowed_roles
            ):
                raise PermissionDenied(
                    "You do not have permission to access this organization."
                )

            request.org_membership = membership
            return view_func(request, *args, **kwargs)

        return _wrapped_view

    return decorator

==> ./app_organizations/middleware.py <==
SESSION_KEY = "switched_org_id"


class CurrentOrganizationMiddleware:
    """
    Attach request.home_org and request.current_org.

    home_org is the org on the user's own employee profile.
    current_org is the same, except for a superuser who has switched
    into another org (its id is kept in the session). The session
    value is ignored for everyone else, and dropped if the org no
    longer exists. Anonymous users, or users without a profile, get None.
    """

    def __init__(self, get_response):
        self.get_response = get_response

    def __call__(self, request):
        request.home_org = None
        request.current_org = None

        user = getattr(request, "user", None)
        if user is not None and user.is_authenticated:
            from appEmp.models import empProfile
            from app_organizations.models import Organization

            profile = (
                empProfile.objects
                .select_related("organization")
                .filter(user=user)
                .first()
            )
            if profile is not None:
                request.home_org = profile.organization
                request.current_org = profile.organization

            if user.is_superuser:
                switched_id = request.session.get(SESSION_KEY)
                if switched_id:
                    try:
                        org = Organization.objects.filter(pk=switched_id).first()
                    except (TypeError, ValueError):
                        org = None
                    if org is None:
                        request.session.pop(SESSION_KEY, None)
                    else:
                        request.current_org = org

        return self.get_response(request)

from django.contrib import messages
from django.contrib.auth.decorators import login_required
from django.core.exceptions import PermissionDenied
from django.shortcuts import redirect, render
from django.views.decorators.http import require_POST

from .forms import CreateOrganizationForm
from .middleware import SESSION_KEY
from .models import Organization
from .services import create_organization


@login_required
def create_org_view(request):
    # Server-side check: only superusers may create organizations.
    if not request.user.is_superuser:
        raise PermissionDenied

    created = None
    form = CreateOrganizationForm(request.POST or None)

    if request.method == "POST" and form.is_valid():
        try:
            org, owner = create_organization(
                name=form.cleaned_data["org_name"],
                owner_email=form.cleaned_data["owner_email"],
                owner_first_name=form.cleaned_data["owner_first_name"],
                owner_last_name=form.cleaned_data["owner_last_name"],
                created_by=request.user,
            )
        except ValueError as exc:
            form.add_error(None, str(exc))
        else:
            created = {"org": org, "owner": owner}
            form = CreateOrganizationForm()

    return render(
        request,
        "app_organizations/create_org.html",
        {"form": form, "created": created},
    )


@login_required
@require_POST
def switch_organization_view(request):
    # Server-side check: only superusers may switch organizations.
    if not request.user.is_superuser:
        raise PermissionDenied

    raw_id = request.POST.get("org_id", "").strip()
    home_org = getattr(request, "home_org", None)

    org = None
    if raw_id:
        org = Organization.objects.filter(pk=raw_id).first() if raw_id.isdigit() else None
        if org is None:
            messages.error(request, "That organization does not exist.")
            return redirect("dashboard")

    # A preview staged in one org must never be confirmed in another.
    request.session.pop("employee_import_rows", None)
    request.session.pop("holiday_import_rows", None)

    if org is None or (home_org is not None and org.pk == home_org.pk):
        request.session.pop(SESSION_KEY, None)
        messages.info(request, "You are back in your own organization.")
    else:
        request.session[SESSION_KEY] = org.pk
        messages.success(request, f"You are now working inside {org.name}.")

    return redirect("dashboard")
